item.content:encoded:
Just did a bit of Wikipedia reading about collective nouns. It's fascinating!

The overall take-away I have of it is that in British English, the use of is/are when it comes to collective nouns like "team" depends on context, and on whether you are emphasising the collective or the individuals.

So in this particular example, I'd lean towards "are" as it's the actions of the individuals within the team that are being described. Whereas, if I were talking about the team directly, such as describing its composition, I might use "is", as it'd feel more natural.

Eg:

Task Force Tau-9 is composed of six members.
Task Force Tau-9 are currently climbing a mountain and drinking beers.

This is a very weird language.

item.content:encoded:
Thank you for the upvote.

Lacking a hook is a common criticism, and I've tried to take it to heart for my later outings (1491 and 1567).

Perhaps, though, one night when you're laying warm in your bed, about to drift off to sleep, this SCP will creep into your thoughts, and you mind will drift to that black, cold tunnel, with the slimy stones under your naked feet, the chilling air sucking the warmth from your skin, the primitive and haunting confusion of waking up to that black silence. Then the blaze of electric light, and the crackling voice trying to be reassuring, but being anything but, then later knowing that they exist, and they know all about this horrible occurance happening to innocent people, and this is but the least of the nightmares that they deal with, and as you shiver in your blanket and clutch your warming cocoa you feel a dark chill descend upon your soul as your view of the world is horribly, irrevocably shaken…

…until the nurse with the soothing voice pushes the needle into your arm and tells you that everything will be okay, you won't remember any of this, you can go back to your peaceful ignorance.

Maybe it's already happened to you?

Sleep well!
